items.t: A $1,500,000 Portfolio in McCormick, PepsiCo and Bristol Myers Squibb Pays $61,489 a Year in Dividends. Here’s What Happens if One Cuts
items.sum: Key TakeawaysA $1,500,000 portfolio split evenly across McCormick, PepsiCo and Bristol Myers Squibb pays about $61,500 a year in dividends at today’s prices, or about $5,120 a month. McCormick and Bristol Myers Squibb each paid out 55% of their free cash flow as dividends over the last twelve months, against 75% for PepsiCo.

items.t: Does PepsiCo (PEP) Change Its Long Term Case With Its Efficiency Reset?
items.sum: PepsiCo (NasdaqGS:PEP) outlined a broad efficiency plan that trims its product portfolio and targets higher operational margins. The company signed a new 10 year beverage and snacks partnership with Hyatt Hotels, covering more than 700 U.S. properties.
